today.headline: Quillon Labs raises €25M Series B for battery diagnostics
today.summary: Berlin-based Quillon Labs, which predicts battery failures from charging data, raised €25 million in a Series B led by Morrow Capital.

card.what_happened: Quillon Labs, a Berlin company that predicts battery failures from charging data, raised €25M in a Series B.
card.why_it_matters: A second large round shows the diagnostics market is maturing — and that the early-stage window for this company has closed.
card.the_company: Quillon Labs sells software that reads charging data from fleets and warns before a battery fails.
card.vc_lesson: By Series B the question is how fast a working model scales, not whether the problem is real.

stories.headline: Stuttgart robotics company Halvard Robotics passes a $1 billion valuation
stories.summary: Halvard Robotics said it had passed a $1 billion valuation after a secondary sale of employee shares to new and existing investors, following a $90 million raise earlier in the year.

card.what_happened: Halvard Robotics, a Stuttgart industrial-robotics company, said it passed a $1 billion valuation (5 Oct 2026), set mainly by employees selling existing shares.
card.why_it_matters: It shows strong investor appetite for robots that small factories can deploy — and it is a late-stage event: the early-stage opportunity was years ago.
card.the_company: Halvard Robotics builds modular industrial robots that mid-sized manufacturers configure for repetitive tasks.
card.vc_lesson: A 'unicorn' headline can come from a secondary share sale: it tells you what buyers paid per share, not how much the company raised.
watch_next: Whether a primary round follows the secondary sale

Today a similar company would most likely surface through the university spinout sensors; by its first funding news the earliest edge was already gone.

concepts.title: What does a valuation mean?
concepts.text: The price of the whole company implied by a deal. A $1B 'unicorn' valuation is a market signal, not cash in the bank — and a small share sale can set it.

concepts.title: Why can a company become a unicorn without a normal round?
concepts.text: A valuation can be set by any priced transaction — including a secondary sale. So 'unicorn' says what buyers paid per share, not how much the company raised.

concepts.title: What is a secondary sale?
concepts.text: Existing shareholders (often employees or early investors) sell shares to new investors. The company receives no new money, but the price sets a new valuation.
